text: This SOP defines the exceptions that must be raised when a vendor invoice is audited against its Purchase Order (PO), Goods Receipt Note (GRN), vendor master record and approval log. Each numbered rule defines exactly one exception and its severity. A finding must cite the number of the rule it relies on. Amounts are in INR and exclude tax.
Rule 2.1.1 (HIGH), amount match. The invoice amount must equal the PO amount. A difference of up to 1% of the PO amount is tolerated. A larger difference, in either direction, is an exception.
Rule 2.1.2 (HIGH), quantity match. The quantity billed on the invoice must not exceed the received quantity recorded on the GRN.

Rule 2.1.3 (HIGH), missing reference. Every invoice must reference a PO and a GRN that exist in the records. An invoice with no PO reference, with no GRN reference, or with a reference that matches no record is an exception.

Rule 2.1.4 (HIGH), receipt remarks. The remarks on a GRN are part of the receipt. If the remarks record that part of the delivery was rejected, damaged beyond use, returned or not delivered, the accepted quantity is reduced by that part. An invoice that bills more than the accepted quantity is an exception, even when the received-quantity field equals the billed quantity. Remarks that confirm that the full quantity was accepted are not an exception.

Rule 2.1.5 (MEDIUM), description match. The goods or services described on the invoice must be those ordered on the PO. Different wording for the same goods or services is acceptable. A description of different goods or services is an exception.
Of two matching invoices, the earlier one is the original. The later one is the duplicate and carries the exception. Duplicates are routed to the Fraud Investigation team.
Rule 2.2.1 (CRITICAL), exact duplicate. An invoice whose invoice number has already been used by an earlier invoice from the same vendor is an exception.

Rule 2.2.2 (CRITICAL), near duplicate. An invoice that bills the same PO and GRN for the same amount as an earlier invoice from the same vendor, under an invoice number that is a re-keyed form of the earlier number (for example changed case, separators or leading zeros, an added suffix, or transposed or substituted characters), is an exception. Consecutive invoice numbers for separate POs and separate deliveries are not duplicates, even when the amounts are equal.
Rule 3.1.1 (MEDIUM), format. The GSTIN on the invoice must be exactly 15 alphanumeric characters.
Rule 3.1.2 (MEDIUM), state code. The first two characters of the GSTIN must be a state code from 01 to 37.
Rule 3.1.3 (HIGH), vendor match. A GSTIN that satisfies Rules 3.1.1 and 3.1.2 must be identical to the GSTIN in the vendor master record. A malformed GSTIN is reported under Rule 3.1.1 or 3.1.2 only.
Rule 4.1.1 (HIGH), same-day splitting. A vendor may have at most 3 invoices dated on the same day. When there are more, every invoice of that vendor dated on that day is an exception.

Rule 4.1.2 (HIGH), structuring across days. Invoices from one vendor for the same goods or services, dated on different days within a short period (as a guide, 7 days), each just below the approval limit of the approver who approved it (as a guide, within 15% of the limit) and together above that limit, are treated as one purchase divided to avoid a higher approval. Every invoice of the group is an exception. A single invoice near a limit is not an exception.
Rule 4.2.1 (MEDIUM), non-business day. Business days are Monday to Friday. An invoice dated on a Saturday or Sunday is an exception.
Rule 4.3.1 (LOW), round amount. An invoice amount that is an exact multiple of INR 10,000 is an exception.
Rule 4.4.1 (CRITICAL), blocked vendor. An invoice from a vendor whose master record is marked blacklisted, or whose GST registration status is Suspended, is an exception.

The approving entry of an invoice is its latest approval-log entry with the action "Approved". Entries with any other action, such as "Escalated", are not approvals. Approver role Approval limit (INR) Manager 100,000 Senior Manager 500,000 Director 2,500,000 CFO 10,000,000
Rule 5.1.1 (CRITICAL), approval limit. An invoice whose amount is greater than the approval limit of the role that approved it is an exception. An amount equal to the limit is within authority.

A finding must propose the next verification step. Three-way match exceptions (2.1.1 to 2.1.5): request proof of delivery from the warehouse manager and hold payment until the difference is explained. Duplicates (2.2.1, 2.2.2): hold payment, confirm with the vendor which invoice is valid, and refer the pair to the Fraud Investigation team. GSTIN exceptions (3.1.1 to 3.1.3): ask the vendor for a corrected invoice and hold payment until it is received. Splitting and structuring (4.1.1, 4.1.2): review all invoices of the group together and obtain approval at the level required for their total. Timing and round amounts (4.2.1, 4.3.1): verify the supporting documents before payment. Blocked vendor (4.4.1): stop payment and refer to Vendor Management. Approval limit (5.1.1): escalate to an approver whose limit covers the amount.

This procedure describes what happens to an invoice after it has been audited against the Procurement & Vendor Auditing SOP: how its risk is scored, who must look at it, and what the reviewer records. It applies to every invoice audited by the pipeline.

A finding states the rule of the SOP that an invoice violates, its severity, and the record fields that show it. A finding comes either from a deterministic control, which compares field values, or from a specialist agent, which reads descriptions, remarks and the other invoices of the vendor. A challenger then tests every agent finding and removes those that the records do not support. Findings from controls are final.

A finding from a control has confidence 1. For a finding from an agent, three things are checked: whether every cited value is in the records, whether the cited rule exists in the active SOP version, and how many of 3 repeated runs of the same agent report the same rule again. The confidence is the mean of the three.

Each finding adds points according to its severity: 30 for critical, 20 for high, 10 for medium and 5 for low, up to a maximum of 100. A critical finding raises the score to at least 70, and a high finding to at least 50. Two scores are computed. The count-based score counts every finding in full. The weighted score counts each finding in proportion to its confidence.

An invoice is approved automatically when its count-based score is below 50. An invoice is escalated to a human reviewer when its weighted score is 50 or more. Payment is held until the review is recorded. An invoice whose count-based score is 50 or more but whose weighted score is below 50 goes to the sampled-review queue. It is not approved automatically. A share of this queue, set by Internal Audit, is reviewed by a human.

The reviewer sees the findings with their evidence, the findings removed by the challenger with the reasons, both scores, and the SOP version applied. The reviewer records one of three decisions, with name and date. Approve: the findings do not prevent payment. Reject: the invoice is not to be paid as submitted. Override: the reviewer sets the findings aside. An override requires a written justification.

For every audited invoice the system keeps an audit pack: the findings with rule, severity, source, confidence and evidence; the removed findings; both scores and the route; the SOP version; and the decision of the reviewer. It also keeps an audit trail with one entry for each stage of the audit. These records are not changed after the decision is recorded.
